title: How RAG works
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers: experiments/logs (audit.json, rag_grid.json, rag_best.json, rag_failures.json, rag_answers/...k10.json record Q-0412) and data/rag_capture.json (live RAG Lab, 3 Nov 2026).

blocks.text: Emma saves a purchase order, and Ledgerline stops her: ERR-PO-0412. What does it mean, and how does she fix it? The answer is in Northbridge's documents.
blocks.say: Emma saves a purchase order, and Ledgerline stops her: error P O, zero four one two. What does it mean, and how does she fix it? The answer is in Northbridge's documents.

blocks.text: Here they are: 693 files of PDFs, spreadsheets, e-mails, service definitions and scans. 4.69 million tokens: far too much to send with every question.
blocks.say: Here they are: six hundred and ninety-three files of PDFs, spreadsheets, e-mails, service definitions and scans. Four point seven million tokens: far too much to send with every question.

blocks.text: First, we parse, with a reader for each kind of file: PDFs keep their pages and headings, and spreadsheet rows keep their column names. All 464 facts we check survive.
blocks.say: First, we parse, with a reader for each kind of file: PDFs keep their pages and headings, and spreadsheet rows keep their column names. All four hundred and sixty-four facts we check survive.

blocks.text: Then we chunk, along each document's own structure: about 200 tokens a piece, with 15 percent overlap. The quick-reference card for this error, QRC-03, becomes three chunks. The whole pile: 28,953.
blocks.say: Then we chunk, along each document's own structure: about two hundred tokens a piece, with fifteen percent overlap. The quick-reference card for this error, Q R C zero three, becomes three chunks. The whole pile: twenty-nine thousand.

blocks.text: Next, two indexes. An embedding model turns each chunk into 384 numbers, a point in space, kept in Chroma. And BM25 remembers which chunks contain which exact words.
blocks.say: Next, two indexes. An embedding model turns each chunk into three hundred and eighty-four numbers, a point in space, kept in Chroma. And B M twenty-five remembers which chunks contain which exact words.

blocks.text: Now Emma's question. In vector space, its nearest neighbours are purchase-order services and ERR-MAT-0412: close in meaning, but the wrong code. BM25 matches the exact words, and puts QRC-03 first.
blocks.say: Now Emma's question. In vector space, its nearest neighbours are purchase-order services and error M A T, zero four one two: close in meaning, but the wrong code. B M twenty-five matches the exact words, and puts Q R C zero three first.

blocks.text: Then a reranker reads the question beside each of the top 20, and puts them in order: 57 milliseconds. A right source in the top five: vectors alone, 56 percent; keywords, 77; keywords and the reranker, 89.
blocks.say: Then a reranker reads the question beside each of the top twenty, and puts them in order: fifty-seven milliseconds. A right source in the top five: vectors alone, fifty-six percent; keywords, seventy-seven; keywords and the reranker, eighty-nine.

blocks.text: The top ten go into the prompt, numbered, and the model answers from them, with citations: a supplier outside the UK needs VAT20-RC, then press F8 again. Search, 45 milliseconds. Answer, 12 seconds.
blocks.say: The top ten go into the prompt, numbered, and the model answers from them, with citations: a supplier outside the U K needs VAT twenty R C, then press F eight again. Search, forty-five milliseconds. Answer, twelve seconds.

blocks.text: That is RAG: parse, chunk, index, search, rerank, answer. 87 percent of the golden set answered correctly, a quarter of a cent each. Its hard case is Emma's Brightcell question, spread over eleven sources. The search finds two.
blocks.say: That is RAG: parse, chunk, index, search, rerank, answer. Eighty-seven percent of the golden set answered correctly, a quarter of a cent each. Its hard case is Emma's Brightcell question, spread over eleven sources. The search finds two.
